record.paper_title: On some open problems related to the restricted Burnside problem.
record.original_question: Suppose G is a topologically finitely generated profinite group. Is the abstract subgroup G^n generated by all nth powers closed? Equivalently, does there exist a function N(m,n) such that for every finite m-generated group K, every element of K^n can be written as a product of at most N(m,n) nth powers of elements of K?

evidence.quote: Section 3 discusses the following problem: Suppose that G is a (topologically) finitely generated profinite group; is the abstract subgroup G^n generated by all nth powers closed? In other words, is there a function N(m,n) such that if K is a finite m-generated group then K^n consists of products of length <=q N(m,n) of nth powers of elements of K?
But the problem remains open for soluble groups.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $G$ be a topologically finitely generated profinite group, and for a positive integer $n$ let $G^n$ denote the abstract (not topologically closed) subgroup of $G$ generated by the set $\{g^n : g \in G\}$ of all $n$-th powers. Decide whether $G^n$ is necessarily closed in $G$. Equivalently, determine whether there exists a function $N(m,n)$ of two positive integer variables such that for every finite $m$-generated group $K$, every element of the verbal subgroup $K^n$ (generated by $n$-th powers in $K$) can be written as a product of at most $N(m,n)$ $n$-th powers of elements of $K$.
artifact.status_search_result: Nikolov and Segal (Annals of Mathematics, 2007, "On finitely generated profinite groups, I: strong completeness and uniform bounds") proved that in every topologically finitely generated profinite group, every subgroup of finite index is open; as a consequence the abstract subgroup G^n generated by n-th powers is closed, and the corresponding uniform bound N(m,n) on the number of n-th powers needed to express elements of K^n in finite m-generated groups K exists. This affirmatively resolves the question.

status_evidence.title: On finitely generated profinite groups, I: strong completeness and uniform bounds
status_evidence.snippet: In a d-generator profinite group the verbal subgroup w(G) is open... in any topologically finitely generated profinite group the subgroups of finite index are open.
status_evidence.claim: Nikolov-Segal proved closedness of verbal subgroups (including G^n) in topologically finitely generated profinite groups, with uniform bounds in finite m-generated groups.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic properties of profinite groups (Segal)
status_evidence.snippet: Given a word w defining a locally finite variety and d, there exists f=f_w(d) such that in every finite d-generator group, each element of w(G) is a product of f w-values.
status_evidence.claim: The uniformity theorem yielding N(m,n) for n-th powers in finite m-generated groups has been established.
